notes: Renal sinus approximated as the hull-enclosed space that is not parenchyma or tumour.

Polar lines here are planes across the kidney's own long axis, not axial CT slices, and one pair serves both R.E.N.A.L. L and PADUA's polar item, though the two systems define their lines differently. PADUA's polar item is middle (2) when more than half the tumour lies between the lines, the rule Wood et al. (BJU Int 2024) used to automate PADUA. So L and PADUA's polar item are approximations.

Sinus estimate implausibly large (62% of the kidney's volume, spanning 61% of its length): the kidney isn't the usual shape, as with a horseshoe or malrotated kidney. The long axis, polar lines and sinus all rest on that shape, so L, N and PADUA's polar, rim and renal-sinus items are unreliable for this kidney.
No vessel mask; hilar suffix not assessed.
